title: Chapter 12: Landforms Created by Wind (Aeolian Geomorphology )

blocks.content: Wind erosion is most effective in arid and semi-arid regions where vegetation cover is minimal and soils are dry and loose.

rows: Horizontal layers of alternating hard and soft rock
Abrasion carves furrows through jointed top hard layer into softer rock beneath
Vertical bands of alternating hard and soft rock parallel to wind
Wind abrasion excavates soft rock bands between resistant hard rocks
Steep-sided overhanging ridges separated by wind-blown troughs

items: Barchans have horns pointing downwind (leeward), whereas Parabolic dunes have horns pointing upwind (windward).
Zeugen develop on horizontal rock strata, while Yardangs form on vertically standing rock strata.
Pediments are gently sloping bedrock surfaces formed at the foot of mountain fronts in arid regions through combined weathering, sheet wash, and wind action.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Wind action is most prominent in arid and semi-arid regions due to sparse vegetation cover and dry, loose surface material.
Deflation creates shallow ground depressions termed blowouts or deflation hollows.
Mushroom rocks (Gours) develop because wind abrasion is most intense close to the ground level.
Barchans are crescent-shaped sand dunes with horns pointing in the downwind (leeward) direction.
Loess deposits consist of fine, unstratified, wind-blown silt transported vast distances from desert source areas.
